from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(reader.pages))
out=Path('tmp/pdfs');out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
pages=[]
for i,page in enumerate(reader.pages,1):
    t=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    pages.append(f'\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n'+t)
text='\\n'.join(pages)
(out/'manuscript.txt').write_text(text)
print(text[:45000])

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import numpy as np
from itertools import combinations
s=1/np.sqrt(2)
X=np.array([[s,s,0.],[-s,s,0.],[0.,0.,1.]])
M=np.array([[0.,0.,2.],[0.,0.,2.],[0.,0.,0.]])
alpha=2.
angles=np.linspace(-np.pi,np.pi,200001)
c=np.cos(angles);v=np.sin(angles)
rot=np.array([[c,v],[-v,c]]).transpose(2,0,1)
ref=np.array([[-c,v],[v,c]]).transpose(2,0,1)
F=lambda Y: np.sum(M*Y)+np.abs(Y).sum()
print('X"'^T X ='"',X.T@X)
print('F(X) =',F(X))
for B in combinations(range(3),2):
    Z=X[list(B)]
    P=M[list(B)]@Z.T
    for name,V in [('rotation',rot),('reflection',ref)]:
        change=np.einsum('tij,ij->t',V-np.eye(2),P)
        change+=np.abs(V@Z).sum(axis=(1,2))-np.abs(Z).sum()
        change+=alpha/2*((V-np.eye(2))**2).sum(axis=(1,2))
        i=change.argmin()
        print('block',tuple(x+1 for x in B),name,'min K(V)-K(I) =',change[i],'theta =',angles[i])
# Construct a combined infinitesimal row rotation that decreases the full objective.
A=np.array([[0.,0.,-1.],[0.,0.,-1.],[1.,1.,0.]])
D=A@X
smooth_dir=(M*D).sum()
nonzero=X"'!=0
nonsmooth_dir=(np.sign(X[nonzero])*D[nonzero]).sum()+np.abs(D[~nonzero]).sum()
print('"'feasible tangent direction D =',D)
print('full directional derivative =',smooth_dir+nonsmooth_dir)
print('critical-point contradiction: G13+G23 >= 2, but symmetry would require G13+G23 = sqrt(2)*G32 <= sqrt(2)')
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from math import sqrt, cos, sin, pi
from itertools import combinations
s=1/sqrt(2)
X=[[s,s,0.],[-s,s,0.],[0.,0.,1.]]
M=[[0.,0.,2.],[0.,0.,2.],[0.,0.,0.]]
alpha=2.
for B in combinations(range(3),2):
    Z=[X[i] for i in B]
    P=[[sum(M[B[i]][q]*Z[j][q] for q in range(3)) for j in range(2)] for i in range(2)]
    z_norm=sum(abs(z) for row in Z for z in row)
    for reflection in (False,True):
        best=(float('inf'),None)
        for q in range(20001):
            theta=-pi+2*pi*q/20000
            c=cos(theta);v=sin(theta)
            V=[[-c,v],[v,c]] if reflection else [[c,v],[-v,c]]
            T=[[V[i][j]-(1 if i==j else 0) for j in range(2)] for i in range(2)]
            delta=sum(T[i][j]*P[i][j]+alpha/2*T[i][j]**2 for i in range(2) for j in range(2))
            delta+=sum(abs(sum(V[i][j]*Z[j][q] for j in range(2))) for i in range(2) for q in range(3))-z_norm
            if delta<best[0]: best=(delta,theta)
        print('block',tuple(i+1 for i in B),'reflection' if reflection else 'rotation','min K(V)-K(I), theta:',best)
print('The simultaneous row-rotation direction with A13=A23=-1 and A31=A32=1 has directional derivative',-2+sqrt(2))
print('Critical-point contradiction: G13+G23 >= 2, whereas symmetry requires G13+G23 = sqrt(2)*G32 <= sqrt(2).')
PY"

strengths: The row-wise orthogonal update preserves feasibility exactly, and the proximal majorization construction provides a useful sufficient-decrease mechanism.
Considering both rotations and reflections appropriately covers the full orthogonal group. Reducing two-row subproblems to one-dimensional optimization is practically appealing.
Experiments cover ten datasets and three PCA formulations, include relevant baselines such as ManPG and RADMM, and report favorable nonnegative-PCA objectives with small constraint violations.
weaknesses: The central stationarity hierarchy, Theorem 3.8(a), is false under the stated assumptions. Equation (38) allows a different subgradient for each block, whereas (39) assumes one subgradient satisfies all blocks simultaneously. A counterexample is n=r=3, f(X)=2(X13+X23), h(X)=||X||1, H=Q=0, α=2, and X=[[s,s,0],[-s,s,0],[0,0,1]], where s=1/√2. Identity globally minimizes every two-row surrogate, yet the feasible curve exp(tA)X, with A=[[0,0,-1],[0,0,-1],[1,1,0]], has objective right derivative √2−2<0 at zero. Thus OBCD can remain at a noncritical BS2 point. This also contradicts Lemma 4.4(b) and the claimed convergence to critical points.

The randomized convergence proofs contain additional substantive errors. In Appendix F.2, equations (51)–(52) replace the newly sampled block B^{t+1} with B^t for a matrix involving X^{t+1}, although X^{t+1} depends on B^t. Equal marginal block distributions do not justify this substitution. Appendix F.4 subsequently uses expectation bounds as pointwise bounds and substitutes the global infimum F∞ for the limiting objective value. Consequently, the stated KL convergence rates are not established.

The main ℓ0 sparse-PCA evaluation uses a trivial optimization regime. Appendix G.2 normalizes ||A||F=1, implying tr(C)=1 and 0≤tr(XᵀCX)≤1. For every tested λ≥10, a feasible matrix with more than r nonzeros has objective at least λ(r+1)−1>λr, while signed coordinate vectors achieve at most λr. Therefore, the global optimum is obtained simply by selecting the r largest diagonal entries of C. This exact baseline is missing, and these experiments do not demonstrate effectiveness on nontrivial sparse-PCA instances.

The exact subproblem solver is incorrect as written. Appendix B lists x_i/y_i as breakpoints for x_i+t y_i=0, which requires −x_i/y_i. It also discards entries with y_i=0, although their ℓ1 contribution λ|x_i|/√(1+t²) depends on t. These issues require correction and validation because global subproblem minimization is essential to the main guarantees.

Experimental controls are insufficient. The ℓ1 comparisons initialize OBCD with an identity matrix but every baseline randomly, confounding performance on these nonconvex objectives. Seed variability, baseline tuning details, and application-level ablations of reflections, surrogate choice, and proximal strength are not reported. Section 5 specifies a 30-second comparison, while Table 1 specifies 40 seconds. These limitations weaken the broad superiority and reproducibility claims.
